A1.justification: Both PDFs describe InsertAnywhere, ROSE++, and VOIBench. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplementary materials are readable and support comparison despite substantial rewriting and reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark comparisons, component ablations, qualitative insertion results, and a 20-participant user study, including supplementary Tables 3–4.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark comparisons, alignment ablations, held-out optical-region measurements, qualitative results, and two user studies in Appendix B.

M1.justification: v2 introduces Optics-Aware Representation Alignment, absent from v1: source–target differences generate extended masks, and intermediate features from ordinary-mask inputs are aligned to a stop-gradient extended-mask branch. This adds a substantive training component beyond v1's ROSE++ LoRA fine-tuning and first-frame conditioning.

E1.justification: The VOI task and ROSE++/VOIBench remain. Appendix B adds a specifically selected shadow/reflection-rich evaluation population for the optics-focused study. The larger VOIBench sample and new held-out ROSE++ split are protocol changes rather than new datasets or general domains.

E2.justification: The main comparison expands from Pika-Pro and Kling to include AnyV2V, ReVideo, Señorita, and VACE with the proposed masks. Table 2 adds ROSE++-fine-tuned VACE controls. The general user study removes Pika-Pro and adds Señorita and VACE; the optics-focused study additionally includes fine-tuned VACE.

E3.justification: VOIBench's stated size changes from 50 to 200 clips, and training increases from 5,000 to 6,500 iterations. New protocols include a 25-sample ROSE++ holdout with region-specific LPIPS/PSNR/SSIM, controlled VACE fine-tuning, and a 30-participant study on 50 optics-rich clips. The existing 20-participant study changes from three to four alternatives.

E4.justification: v2 adds alignment-loss ablations, fine-mask versus extended-mask attention analysis, optical-region measurements, unedited-background fidelity checks, and an optics-focused perceptual study. The progressive ablation drops v1's initial camera-only configuration and adds alignment. Reference-crop and scene-flow analyses are retained; moving the latter into the main text is not a new analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. v2 calls the motion-smoothness gap within per-clip noise but supplies no uncertainty estimate or statistical procedure supporting that statement.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces the full model's CLIP-I/DINO-I/imaging-quality scores of 0.8122/0.5678/0.7101 with 0.8132/0.5669/0.7473, adds baseline results, and drops commercial multi-view entries. Commercial scores on retained metrics are unchanged. New Table 4 reports optics-region PSNR of 19.9065 without alignment versus 27.2362 with alignment. User-study and qualitative results also change substantially. Revised settings prevent interpreting cross-version differences as like-for-like performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 adds a mathematical definition of the extended-mask feature-alignment loss with a stop-gradient target in Equation 7. Other equations largely expand or restate existing placement, scene-flow aggregation, reprojection, and reference-selection procedures. Neither version provides theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list make Optics-Aware Representation Alignment a new central contribution and explicitly claim to open-source ROSE++. The geometric-placement and dataset-construction claims remain. Calling ROSE++ a quadruplet dataset clarifies the four components already described in v1 rather than establishing a new dataset structure.

C2.justification: v1 attributes shadows outside the mask and lighting adaptation to ROSE++ LoRA fine-tuning. v2 argues that fine-tuning alone remains insufficient and attributes these effects to representation alignment, supported by new attention and regional-fidelity interpretations. It also adds an explicit limitation excluding complex physical interactions, such as a heavy object deforming a soft sofa.

D1.justification: Appendix A adds extended-mask cleanup instructions and B200 inference time and memory measurements. Reported training changes from 5,000 iterations/40 hours to 6,500 iterations/60 hours, while v1's 50-denoising-step disclosure disappears. Appendix D specifies inputs supplied to new baselines. v2 states ROSE++ is open source but supplies no dataset access link.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to OmniInsert, ReVideo, and Señorita-2M and removes several image-insertion and general-video references. Related work is refocused around mask-free versus mask-conditioned VOI, elaborating a distinction already present in v1's method overview rather than introducing an entirely new research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten around geometric grounding and optics-aware synthesis. ROSE++ construction moves inside the synthesis section, and the supplement gains explicit A–D organization. The title, terminology, author order, and equal-contribution designation also change.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column presentation. v2 adds alignment-architecture, attention-map, and user-study displays; replaces many qualitative comparison panels; and restructures comparison tables. The existing scene-flow illustration and quantitative component-ablation table move from the supplement into the main text.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for the central optical-effects claim through same-data VACE controls, held-out regional measurements, alignment ablations, and an optics-focused user study. These address v1's reliance on qualitative lighting examples and commercial-only comparisons. Clearer mechanism documentation and explicit limitations also help. Benchmark accounting remains unclear because commercial scores are unchanged despite the stated expansion, and statistical uncertainty remains unreported, but these gaps do not outweigh the substantial gains in controlled evidence.
